Lessons.Title: Does It Make Sense?
ExplanationParagraphs: The original 2021 lesson Does It Make Sense? combines mental computation, reasonable estimation and two-step addition/subtraction word problems. It does NOT ask merely for isolated hundreds rounding.

Warm-up — True or False: Is it Greater? (10 min). Compare 132+115>200 (247>200 true), 228+195>400 (423>400 true) and 217+151>400 (368>400 false). Students explain their mental checks rather than enter a Boolean without reasons.

Activity 1 — Quick Estimates (15 min). Priya starts with212 beads, uses98 and adds308: total422. Her estimate about400 is reasonable. Explain a mental approximation such as 200−100+300≈400 while keeping the exact 422 separate.

Clare has252 beads, uses92, receives203: exact363, quick estimate250−90+200≈360. Han combines558 with302 then uses250: exact610, quick estimate560+300−250≈610. A valid rounding strategy need not match the exact answer perfectly.

Activity 2 — Solve and Reason (20 min). Jada begins326, gives32 and uses84: 326−32−84=210. Noah uses624 beads on Monday, 132 more Tuesday and48 Wednesday: 624+132+48=804. Students choose one, show their own strategy, exchange work and judge if a partner answer makes sense.

Discussion, estimating, selecting a strategy and comparing a partner's work must be assessed by a teacher. Only the eight exact numerical anchors can be machine-checked without losing the intent. No publisher bead photo or restricted original Beads in the Bin Cool-down is reproduced.

KeyConcepts.Title: Reasonableness
KeyConcepts.Definition: A rough estimate checks whether a precise computed result has the right magnitude.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Choose appropriate benchmark arithmetic but do not confuse rounded and exact.

KeyConcepts.Title: Sequential changes
KeyConcepts.Definition: Addition adds received pieces; subtraction removes used or gifted pieces.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Read the story chronology and preserve sign at every change.

KeyConcepts.Title: Mental comparison
KeyConcepts.Definition: Compare sums with a threshold without necessarily completing a long algorithm.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Related benchmark values can prove true or false with explanations.

KeyConcepts.Title: Partner reasoning
KeyConcepts.Definition: Judge whether another solution's strategy and numerical result agree with the source story.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Teacher reviews all free-form checks and diagrams.

WorkedExamples.Title: Priya estimate
WorkedExamples.Question: Is 400 a reasonable estimate for 212−98+308?
Steps: 422 is close enough to400 to justify the rough estimate.
WorkedExamples.Check: Do not mark400 as the exact count.

WorkedExamples.Title: Jada two-step change
WorkedExamples.Question: What remains from326 after giving32 and using84?
WorkedExamples.Check: A result greater than326 would be suspect.

WorkedExamples.Title: Noah three days
WorkedExamples.Question: How many beads did Noah use over three days 624,132,48?
WorkedExamples.Check: All source contributions added exactly once.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat an estimate of400 as precise answer422.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source asks separately if the estimate makes sense; numerical precision is different.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Subtract 308 for Priya because she had used beads earlier.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The 308 beads were placed BACK in the bag, not used.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: For Noah subtract the Tuesday/Wednesday beads.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: He uses additional beads each day, and the question is total used.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Grade partner explanation from scalar result alone.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source asks for reasonableness and a demonstration of method.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher reviews logic, estimates and arithmetic.

SummaryPoints: Source bead totals Priya422, Clare363, Han610, Jada210, Noah804.
Estimate and exact result are different claims; compare approximate magnitude.
Source photo not copied and gated Cool-down not claimed.
